result.title: MedGuardBench: A Patient-Oriented Benchmark for Personalized Guardrail Development
result.summary: Safety is personal: the same action can be safe for one person but unsafe for another. Yet current guardrails judge content without considering who is affected. Using medication safety, we introduce \textit{patient-conditioned medication guarding}, which predicts a safety verdict and 17 risk categories from a patient profile and prescription. We release \textbf{MedGuardBench}, a drug-disjoint benchmark of 5{,}001 scenarios across 87 medications. We find that standard guardrails rely on surface cues, such as wording and profile presence, rather than patient facts. To address this, we develop \textit{personalized reasoning guardrails} with three components. \textbf{Personalized Reasoning Distillation} links risks to relevant patient fields. \textbf{Context Unrolling (CU)} makes models check each field themselves, reducing false alarms on most backbones; controls show that providing the check does not yield the same benefit. A \textbf{rule-based reward (guided GRPO)} improves unsafe recall and complex-risk detection, including allergies and adverse reactions, on some backbones, but increases false alarms on others. Our models outperform base models and matched no-profile controls in accuracy, while reducing false alarms relative to no-profile controls. Profile removal and swapping confirm that gains come from patient information, not fine-tuning alone.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「患者条件化的用药安全判别」任务，发布覆盖 5001 个场景、87 种药物的 drug-disjoint 基准 MedGuardBench，指出现有 guardrail 依赖措辞、是否附带档案等表面线索，并给出个性化推理 guardrail：风险与患者字段关联的蒸馏、逐字段自检的 Context Unrolling 以及规则奖励的 guided GRPO。
AI.relevance_reason: 其逐字段 Context Unrolling 与「提供检查但不强制自检」的对照、以及删除/互换患者档案的增益归因，可能为 LVR 中证明模型确实使用视觉证据、以及显式证据筛选与监督归因提供可核查线索。
